item.title: Essential Components for Building Human-Like AI Assistants
item.author: aldrinjenson@gmail.com (Aldrin Jenson)
item.description:
In this article, I’ll explore the key components that I believe are essential for current Large Language Models (LLMs) to function effectively as AI assistants or agents. Based on my analysis, there are five core elements, plus one bonus feature, that bring us really close to creating truly human-like AI assistants.

Core Components

1. Computer Interaction Capabilities

The LLM should be able to navigate computers and browsers just as a human would. This fundamental ability enables the AI to interact with digital interfaces naturally and effectively.

Ref: OpenAI operator, Hyperbrowser

2. Robust Coding Environment

Rather than judging an AI assistant by its pre-built tools, we should evaluate its ability to create tools in real-time using a coding environment like Python. This environment should enable the AI to write functions for specific tasks, such as making API calls to fetch data, and create reusable tools as needed.

Ref: Task builder in Athena Intelligence which lets the AI write code to save new tools that it can use

3. Voice Communication

An ideal AI assistant shouldn’t be limited to text-based interactions. Like a human executive assistant, it should be capable of natural and efficient voice communication, making interactions more intuitive and accessible.

Ref: OpenAIs real-time Voice mode

4. Context Awareness and Memory

Personalization is crucial for an effective AI assistant. The system should maintain context through vector embeddings of past interactions and user preferences, allowing it to learn from experience and apply this knowledge in future sessions.

Ref: Graphiti by Zep or normal RAG of learnings -> with memories injected to context for every new human message.

Ideally there should be a tool the agent can call to save learnings to the graph or Embedding space whenever required. I think for every human message, the right memories are fetched from the vector space and given as probable context.

5. Real-time Feedback Loop

For managing long-running tasks, a robust feedback system is essential. The LangChain framework demonstrates this well with its messaging system. When handling extended tasks, the tool should:

  • Provide immediate acknowledgment (e.g., “Task initiated”) by yielding a Tool Response Msg
  • Offer a function handler/listener for progress monitoring — that the agent can call at any later time to check progress
  • Once the long-running task is done, inject the output as a ToolResponse message — The llms with their increasingly large context windows would be smart enough to associate the responce with the originally called tool.

Ref: Langchain’s ToolResponse message

Bonus Feature: Task Branching

An additional powerful capability would be task branching or forking. This feature would allow the agent to:

  • Create separate execution threads while maintaining full context
  • Work independently on specific tasks
  • Report back to the main thread upon completion
  • Continue main operations uninterrupted while ensuring that every branched task has full context of everything till previous flow Ref: num_past_messages = infinity for subagents in Athena Agents

This mirrors how a human team member might take on an assigned task, work independently, and report back upon completion.

These components, when implemented effectively, bring us much closer to creating AI assistants that can truly emulate human-like capabilities and interactions.

I strongly feel that the system built and improved at Athena Intelligence will be one of the first ones that can truly achieve the incredible feat of making a near identical AI assistant.

Credits: The AI system — Winston from the novel Origin, by Dan Brown

item.title: I wrote a poem in 10 minutes!
item.author: aldrinjenson@gmail.com (Aldrin Jenson)
item.description:
Yes chatGPT is involved. But way lesser than you think.

What happened

Inspiration randomly stuck and I wrote this poem within 2-3 minutes (Yes, I noted the time. It’s definitely lesser than 4 minutes).

Oh what is love,
but a fleeting romance
Oh, what is anger,
but a fleeting moment of rage..

Oh what is passion,
but a fleeting glimpse of action
Oh what is disgust,
but a fleeting moment of distate

Oh, in this world, what is real
but not a fleeting moment of emotion
Oh why do we care so much
for something that is fleeting..

Oh, for validation and appreciation
isn't worth the subjugation
Oh, for anger and annoyance,
isn't worth the pain

Everything is temporary
Everything is fleeting
Why hurt yourself
Trying so hard
in this fleeting world..

It’s a short about the fleeting momentary thing in life, proving that in the end everything is fleeting, so why care so much about anything in particular.

Now, after a few hours, I randomly thought, why don’t I just put it into chatGPT and see if it can improve. This was the prompt:

This is a short poem I wrote in less than a minute about the fleeting momentary feelings of life, proving that in the end everything is fleeting, so why care so much about others. What do you think? How to improve? [Paste poem here]

This was the response:

Your poem captures the essence of fleeting emotions and the transient nature of life. Here are a few suggestions to enhance it:

Oh, what is love,
but a fleeting dance of hearts
Oh, what is anger,
but a fleeting storm that departs

Oh, what is passion,
but a fleeting flame that ignites
Oh, what is disgust,
but a fleeting shadow that bites

In this vast world, what is real,
but fleeting moments we borrow
Why then obsess and cling,
to what brings only sorrow

Validation and appreciation,
not worth sacrificing our worth
Anger and annoyance,
not worth the pain we unearth

Everything in life is transient,
like ripples in the wind
Why exhaust ourselves chasing,
what soon begins to rescind

Embrace the fleeting nature,
with a heart light and free
For in acceptance we find solace,
and true contentment shall be.

Mind = Blown🤯

I was blown away by the response. It rightly added rhyming schemes while correctly keeping the message of the poem.

I tried one more variation that was okayish, but nothing too spectacular as this one.

So I then took parts from both and rewrote some lines myself to finally I have this final piece that took all around 10 minutes in total, right from the writing phase. Here goes:

Fleeting

Oh, what is love,
but a fleeting dance of hearts
Oh, what is anger,
but a fleeting storm that departs

Oh, what is passion,
but a fleeting flame that ignites
Oh, what is disgust,
but a fleeting shadow that bites

In this vast world, what is real,
but fleeting moments we borrow
Why then hold on so tightly,
to what slips away so fast?

Validation and appreciation,
mere whispers in the breeze
Anger and annoyance,
like waves upon the seas

Everything in life is transient,
like ripples in the wind
Why exhaust ourselves chasing,
what soon begins to rescind

So embrace the fleeting nature,
with a heart light and free
For in acceptance we find solace,
and contentment shall ours be.

- Aldrin Jenson and ChatGPT

Afterthoughts

I think this revolution of AI tools going on right now is awesome. I have never studied any formal music or song writing. In fact I have ever written only a handful of writings that can even borderline be close to a poem.

But now, I was able to jot down my ideas and chatGPT gave me a piece of writing that I am quite happy to share with others and convey the same feelings and ideas I wanted to convey with them.


I asked chatGPT in a fresh chat instance to write a poem about: the fleeting momentary feelings of life proving that in the end everything is fleeting, so why care so much about others.

But this one turned out to be extremely different from the key aspects I came up with. Thus, my point being is that, with AI tools like chatGPT, the common man can now do things like an average trained person. Of course chatGPT can never make me a professional song writer (yet🤞). There may be people who are more capable, but maybe chatGPT can give me average performance to proudly share my ideas as a poem or a literature work without being too embarrassed about conveying the idea through a poem at all due to the fear of being judged at the poor writing skills? Maybe, whatever teh case, I think this is a win for a poem written in just 10 minutes :)
